key_insight: In coronene graphene quantum dots, SevenNet systematically underestimates vacancy formation energies, with larger mean deficits as more edge C–H bonds are broken.
engineering_relevance: SevenNet can support rapid defect-structure screening and preliminary ranking, but absolute vacancy energies and multi-basin edge configurations need DFT validation.
method: Benchmark SevenNet (7net-omni-i12) against spin-polarized PBE DFT using GPAW.
Evaluate monovacancy, divacancy, and Stone–Wales defects in coronene (C24H12).
Compare 28 matched vacancy reconstructions using self-consistent chemical-potential reservoirs.
evidence_signal: SevenNet underestimates all 28 matched vacancy formation energies, with mean deficits of 0.30–0.74 eV for monovacancies and 0.65–1.11 eV for divacancies; mean Stone–Wales energies differ by only 0.013 eV.
watch_item: These findings are specific to the coronene benchmark; monitor symmetry-equivalent energy spreads for basin-sensitive relaxation behavior.
paper_title: Edge-scaling softening of a universal machine-learned potential: point-defect formation energies in a coronene graphene quantum dot
